Basic Types of Cells
2basic typesof cells:
Prokaryotes: organisms that lackmembrane-bound nucleus and membrane-bound organelles
DNA concentrated in an area called nucleoid
Divided into 2 Domains: Bacteria& Archaea
Bacteria: organisms that are similar to first cellular life forms
Archaea: organisms more closely related to eukaryotic cells
Eukaryotes: organisms composed of one or more cells that havea nucleus & membrane-bound organelles
Organelle: sub-cellular structure; well-defined, intracellular bodies that perform specific functions for the cell
Perform functions for the cell as organs perform functions for the body
Cells generally largerthan those of prokaryotes
explanation: Cells are classified into two basic types: prokaryotes and eukaryotes. Prokaryotes lack a membrane-bound nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; their DNA is concentrated in a region called the nucleoid. Prokaryotes are divided into two domains: Bacteria (which are similar to the first cellular life forms) and Archaea (which are more closely related to eukaryotes). Eukaryotes are organisms composed of one or more cells that contain a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles. Organelles are sub-cellular intracellular bodies that perform specific functions, analogous to organs in a body. Eukaryotic cells are generally larger than prokaryotic cells.

questions.q: Where is the DNA concentrated in prokaryotic cells?
questions.exp: In prokaryotes, the DNA is concentrated in a region called the nucleoid.

questions.q: Which two Domains contain prokaryotic organisms?
questions.exp: Prokaryotes are divided into two Domains: Bacteria and Archaea.
